ground_truth: The problem is that the people can't get their hands on it. When you turn around and get upset over what's going on with both Iran and Venezuela, the election is not going to be until 18 months, and by that time, these threats may have subsided, and you've got domestic issues that you're focused on. So that's the shortcoming of our electoral process, where you only vote two, four, and six years, and when you vote, you give your power away to your representatives, who then have a monopoly on lawmaking, and law is the central core of society, of civilization. It's the law that we live under. And so what we need to do is to find a way to do that. Find a way to get beyond the monopoly that representatives have in lawmaking. And what I've come up with, after 30 years of effort, is a manual that will be published next summer that provides the details of how the people can become lawmakers by amending the Constitution and by enacting a law, the Legislative Procedures Act. If people are making laws, it has to be done in a deliberative fashion. You just can't put something in front of them, like Brexit, something very complex and nuanced, and put it in front of them and they vote their gut, almost 50-50. And so now you have the government saying, oh, we can't interrupt the decision of the people. Well, Tom Oliver had it right, the comedian, and that was that what the parliament should do is run. Is recognize that the referendum was flawed, was wrong, and dismiss it, and just move on and forget Brexit. But no, these politicians get so steep in their thinking that they can't show any kind of judgment to improve the situation. So we'll see what happens with Brexit. But the approach was totally wrong. And Cameron should be... should be charged with criminality for what he did in kicking the can improperly down the road. So my response to the issues that face us as a nation, I don't see them readily solvable. I'll give you an example. Supposing Bernie Sanders, who's my choice, gets elected and appoints Chelsea Gabbard as his vice president. Lo and behold, they have an agenda. Well? I would guess that there'll be at least, even if the Democrats take over the Senate in 2020, there'll still be more than 40 that will be there. So any of the agenda items that pass the House will be thwarted and sabotaged in the Senate. So if that's the case, and they want to get their agenda, Bernie and Chelsea want to get their agenda enacted, the way to do it is to go ahead and permit the people to have an election to amend the Constitution, giving them the power to have a legislature of the people, and then pass the Legislative Procedures Act so that they exercise their power to make laws in a very deliberative fashion. That's my solution to the situation we have today.
